I farm in Quzhou County, so I will stay with the system I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That matches my local climate, my age, my experience, and the equipment and labor I can manage. I do not want to take big risks on vegetables, cotton, or specialty crops because they need more market timing, more labor, and closer technical management. Grain is steadier for me. I will plant improved winter wheat because it is reliable and easier for me to manage than chasing very high-input options. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid summer maize because hybrid maize gives me stronger yield and better stability here. For field management, I will keep fertilization moderate and practical, with more nutrient going to maize because it responds strongly and follows wheat in the rotation. I will use ploughing before wheat to reset the field and bury residue well, then rotary tillage before maize so I can turn the crop around quickly after wheat harvest. I will irrigate wheat more times because spring drought is common for us, while maize will get fewer irrigations and depend partly on summer rain. I will spray only as much as needed to control the main diseases, insects, and weeds, because I want to control costs and avoid unnecessary passes. My goal is stable yield, manageable work, and low production risk across the full year.
